summary: Postel assigns ranges of host-host protocol link numbers for the Message Switching Protocol experiment, for network measurement under the UCLA Network Measurement Center, and for private experiments, and corrects the link assignment table. It was replaced by RFC 604.

eli5.summary: A table that says which numbered lanes on the network are reserved for which experiments. It was later replaced by a newer table.

subtitle: Assignments of link numbers for Message Switching Protocol and network measurement.

tldr.problem: The Host-Host Protocol needed to allocate specific link numbers for experimental protocols and for measuring network performance.
tldr.mechanism: Jon Postel assigned ranges of link numbers (0-255) to different purposes: control, connections, reserved use, measurement work at UCLA, and the Message Switching Protocol experiment.
tldr.outcome: This allocation ensured that experiments and measurements could proceed without interfering with regular communication and provided a framework for future assignments. It was superseded by RFC 604 with updated policies.

today: RFC 317 was replaced by RFC 604 as the ARPANET evolved and more formal protocols were defined. The role of allocating resource numbers has been taken over by IANA (Internet Assigned Numbers Authority) in the modern internet.

sections.title: Link Number Allocation
sections.content:
Jon Postel at UCLA-NMC assigns link numbers in the Host-Host Protocol to support experimental work and network measurement. Link numbers are one way the protocol identifies different communication streams between hosts. The ARPANET's protocol design allocated 256 link numbers (0-255), and this RFC defines how they are to be used.

Three new assignments are made: links for the Message Switching Protocol experiment, links for network measurement under the UCLA Network Measurement Center, and corrected allocations for regular use.
sections.eli5: Different experiments on the network need different numbered channels to talk on so they don't interfere with each other. Postel decides which numbers go to which projects.

sections.title: Link Range Assignments
sections.content:
Link 0 is reserved as the control link. Links 2-71 are available for regular connections. Links 1 and 72-158 are reserved for future use. Links 159-191 are assigned for network measurement work directed by the UCLA Network Measurement Center. Links 192-195 are assigned for the Message Switching Protocol (MSP) experiment. Links 196-255 are available for private experimental use.

This allocation balances the needs of operational network communication with the requirements for measurement and experimental protocols being tested on the ARPANET.
sections.eli5: Link 0 is for control, 2-71 for normal talking, 159-191 for measuring how the network works, 192-195 for a special experiment, and 196-255 for other experiments.

sections.title: Purpose and Impact
sections.content:
By allocating specific ranges for measurement and experiments, this RFC allows the ARPANET team to study network performance and test new protocols without disrupting operational traffic. The 32-link range for measurement (159-191) was particularly important, as understanding network behavior required substantial instrumentation.

The assignment also corrects an earlier document (NIC 8246) that had listed the allocations incorrectly, ensuring all sites use the same definitions.
sections.eli5: The measurement team could look at what was happening on the network using their assigned links. The Message Switching experiment had its own links too. Everyone using the same plan meant nothing got confused.
